title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཛ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 98)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio, Madhyamaka section vol. ཛ; the page is a Buddhist refutation of hereditary Brahmin caste (consistent with Bhāviveka's Tarkajvālā in this volume).

tr_errors_A.english: This was taught by the <term>Rishi</term> <gloss>Sage</gloss> Shanti.
tr_errors_A.problem: ཤེད is Manu (the lawgiver); 'Shanti' is a wrong name, so the cited authority of the donkey/pig/dog verse is misidentified

tr_errors_A.english: there are those of Brahmin lineage who became Kshatriyas by holding territory
tr_errors_A.problem: ཡུལ་འཁོར་འཛིན is the proper name Dhṛtarāṣṭra; read as a common phrase, the named example is lost and an invented mechanism ('by holding territory') is supplied

tr_errors_A.english: Ten servants of the tenth city
tr_errors_A.problem: place name Daśapura rendered literally as 'the tenth city'

tr_errors_A.english: It is extremely difficult to prove the purity of a lineage.
tr_errors_A.problem: the causal link 'because of this [verse]' is dropped, detaching the conclusion from the verse

tr_errors_A.english: it is often not counted as a fault
tr_errors_A.problem: 'often' is added; the source says it is not counted as a fault

tr_errors_A.english: If you claim that caste is inherent to a Brahmin
tr_errors_A.problem: the thesis is that birth-caste is what makes one a Brahmin; 'inherent to a Brahmin' slightly skews it

tr_errors_B.english: And nine sprigs of <term>dūrvā</term> <gloss>sacred ritual</gloss> grass in the pleasure grove
tr_errors_B.problem: the print reads དག (plural marker), not དགུ 'nine'; the number appears to be added (low confidence at this resolution)

tr_errors_B.english: Such verses were taught by Sage Manu and others.
tr_errors_B.problem: ལ་སོགས་པ qualifies the verses ('these and similar verses'), not Manu; 'and others' is misattached

other.note: A's <summary> says the author argues 'behavior and character ... should define one's status', which is more than this page states (it only refutes birth as the cause of Brahminhood)

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error, but B correctly identifies Manu, Daśapura, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vyāsa and Viśvāmitra and keeps the verse structure and causal links, while A misnames the authority and turns Dhṛtarāṣṭra into a vague phrase.

book_verdict: A clean, accurately transcribed Derge folio of a Buddhist critique of hereditary caste; both translations get the argument right, and B is better on proper names and structure.
